paper.title: GUIDE-Seq enables genome-wide profiling of off-target cleavage by CRISPR-Cas nucleases
paper.shortTitle: GUIDE-Seq enables genome-wide profiling of off-target cleavage
paper.authors: TsaiShengdar Q., ZhengZongli, NguyenNhu T. et al.

thesis: Our experiments define the most rigorous framework for genome-wide identification of RGN off-target effects to date and provide a method for evaluating the safety of these nucleases prior to clinical use.

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: Which intervention or mechanism produces the reported experimental effect?

nodes.title: Choose construct and controls
nodes.body: CRISPR RNA-guided nucleases (RGNs) are widely used genome-editing reagents, but methods to delineate their genome-wide off-target cleavage activities have been lacking.

nodes.title: Run assays against controls
nodes.body: Here we describe an approach for global detection of DNA double-stranded breaks (DSBs) introduced by RGNs and potentially other nucleases.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: Finally, GUIDE-Seq revealed that truncated guide RNAs exhibit substantially reduced RGN-induced off-target DSBs.

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: Our experiments define the most rigorous framework for genome-wide identification of RGN off-target effects to date and provide a method for evaluating the safety of these nucleases prior to clinical use.
